metadata.title: On Response-Adaptive Targeting Strategies for Multi-Treatment Experiments

nodes.name: Assignment vector
nodes.statement: For each patient $m \ge 1$, the \emph{assignment vector} $X_m = (X_{m,1}, \dots, X_{m,K})$ takes values in $\{0,1\}^K$ and satisfies $\sum_{k=1}^K X_{m,k} = 1$. The event $\{X_{m,k} = 1\}$ means that patient $m$ is assigned to arm $k$.
nodes.label: def:assignment

nodes.name: Responses and parameters
nodes.statement: For each arm $k \in [K]$, $\{\xi_{m,k} : m \ge 1\}$ is a sequence of i.i.d.\ real random variables, the potential responses of patients on treatment $k$. The parameter of interest for arm $k$ is the mean $\theta_k := \mathbb{E}[\xi_{1,k}]$, and $\Theta = (\theta_1, \dots, \theta_K) \in \mathbb{R}^K$. We write $V_k := \mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}[\xi_{1,k}]$ for the variance of the response of arm $k$.
nodes.label: def:responses

nodes.name: Allocation counts
nodes.statement: The number of patients assigned to arm $k$ up to time $n$ is \[ N_{n,k} := \sum_{j=1}^n X_{j,k}, \qquad N_n := (N_{n,1}, \dots, N_{n,K}). \] The vector $N_n / n$ is the \emph{observed allocation proportion} at time $n$.
nodes.label: def:counts

nodes.name: Counts sum to time
nodes.statement: For all $n \ge 1$, $\sum_{k=1}^K N_{n,k} = n$, and hence $\sum_{k=1}^K \frac{N_{n,k}}{n} = 1$.
nodes.label: lem:counts_sum

nodes.statement: Immediate from $\sum_{k=1}^K X_{j,k} = 1$ and summing over $j \le n$.

nodes.name: Filtration
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}_m := \sigma\big((X_i, \xi_i)_{1 \le i \le m}\big)$ is the filtration generated by the assignments and observed outcomes of the first $m$ patients, with $\mathcal{F}_0$ the trivial $\sigma$-algebra.
nodes.label: def:filtration

nodes.name: RAR procedure
nodes.statement: A \emph{response-adaptive randomization (RAR) procedure} is a sequence $(p_m)_{m \ge 1}$ of $\mathcal{F}_m$-measurable random vectors taking values in the probability simplex \[ \Delta_K := \Big\{ p \in [0,1]^K : \sum_{k=1}^K p_k = 1 \Big\}, \] such that the assignment $X_{m+1}$ is drawn conditionally on $\mathcal{F}_m$ according to $p_m$: \[ \mathbb{P}(X_{m+1} = k \mid \mathcal{F}_m) = p_{m,k}, \qquad k \in [K]. \]
nodes.label: def:rar

nodes.name: Target function and target allocation
nodes.statement: A \emph{target function} is a map $\rho : \mathcal{H} \to \Delta_K$ defined on an open domain $\mathcal{H} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^K$, written $\rho(z) = (\rho_1(z), \dots, \rho_K(z))$ with $\sum_{k=1}^K \rho_k(z) = 1$. The \emph{target allocation} is $v := \rho(\Theta)$. A RAR procedure is an \emph{adaptive targeting mechanism} if $N_n/n \to v$.
nodes.label: def:target

nodes.name: Sequential estimator
nodes.statement: Given initial values $\theta_{0,k} \in \mathbb{R}$, the sequential estimator of $\theta_k$ at stage $m$ is \[ \hat{\theta}_{m,k} := \frac{\sum_{j=1}^m X_{j,k}\, \xi_{j,k} + \theta_{0,k}}{N_{m,k} + 1}. \] We write $\hat{\Theta}_m := (\hat{\theta}_{m,1}, \dots, \hat{\theta}_{m,K})$.
nodes.label: def:estimator

nodes.name: Plug-in target
nodes.statement: The plug-in estimator of the target allocation is $\hat{\rho}_m := \rho(\hat{\Theta}_m)$, with components $\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$. It is well defined once $\hat{\Theta}_m \in \mathcal{H}$, which is guaranteed by Condition~\ref{def:condB}.
nodes.label: def:plugin_target

nodes.name: Bahadur representation
nodes.statement: An estimator $\hat{\theta}_{m,k}$ of $\theta_k$ admits a \emph{Bahadur representation} if \[ \hat{\theta}_{m,k} = \frac{1}{N_{m,k}}\sum_{j=1}^m X_{j,k}\, \xi_{j,k} + o\!\big(N_{m,k}^{-1/2}\big), \qquad m \to \infty. \]
nodes.label: def:bahadur

nodes.name: The sequential estimator is Bahadur
nodes.statement: On the event $\{N_{m,k} \to \infty\}$, the estimator of Definition~\ref{def:estimator} admits the Bahadur representation of Definition~\ref{def:bahadur}. The formalized statement \texttt{estimator\_sub\_eq} is the sharper \emph{exact} error identity \[ \hat{\theta}_{m,k} - \theta_k = \frac{Q_{m,k} + (\theta_{0,k} - \theta_k)}{N_{m,k} + 1}, \] which holds pathwise for every $m$ (with $N_{m,k}+1 \ne 0$, automatic for $\{0,1\}$-indicators) and from which the $o(N^{-1/2})$ Bahadur form is immediate.
nodes.label: lem:estimator_bahadur

nodes.statement: The numerator of $\hat{\theta}_{m,k} - \theta_k = \frac{\sum_j X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} + \theta_{0,k}}{N_{m,k} + 1} - \theta_k$ is $\sum_j X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} + \theta_{0,k} - \theta_k(N_{m,k}+1) = (\sum_j X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} - \theta_k N_{m,k}) + (\theta_{0,k} - \theta_k) = Q_{m,k} + (\theta_{0,k} - \theta_k)$, giving the exact identity. On $\{N_{m,k}\to\infty\}$ the offset $\frac{\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k}{N_{m,k}+1} = O(N_{m,k}^{-1}) = o(N_{m,k}^{-1/2})$, which is the Bahadur form.

nodes.name: Condition A: second moments
nodes.statement: Condition~\textbf{A} holds if for every arm $k \in [K]$ the response satisfies $\mathbb{E}|\xi_{1,k}|^2 < \infty$ (equivalently $V_k < \infty$).
nodes.label: def:condA

nodes.name: Attainable parameter values
nodes.statement: For each arm $k$, let $V_k^{\mathrm{att}}$ be the set of all values attainable by the estimator $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}$, over all $n$ and all realizations of the responses $\{\xi_{j,k}\}$, and set $I_k := \{\theta_k\} \cup V_k^{\mathrm{att}}$. (The formalized \texttt{AlphaRAR.attainableSet} is the \emph{closure} of the range of $\hat{\theta}_{\cdot,k}$ over all times and outcomes; being closed it already contains every a.s.\ limit $z_k$ — in particular $\theta_k$ on the infinitely-sampled event — so the explicit union with $\{\theta_k\}$ is unnecessary.)
nodes.label: def:attainable

nodes.name: Condition B: regular non-sparse target
nodes.statement: Condition~\textbf{B} holds if the domain $\mathcal{H}$ is open and contains $I_1 \times \dots \times I_K$, and moreover \begin{itemize} \item $\rho$ is twice differentiable on $\mathcal{H}$; \item for every $z \in I_1 \times \dots \times I_K$, $\rho(z) \in (0,1)^K$. \end{itemize} In particular the target allocation $v = \rho(\Theta)$ is non-sparse: $v_k > 0$ for all $k$.
nodes.label: def:condB

nodes.name: Sparse target allocation
nodes.statement: A target function $\rho$ is \emph{sparse at $\Theta$} if some component of $v = \rho(\Theta)$ is zero.
nodes.label: def:sparse

nodes.name: $o_p$ and $O_p$
nodes.statement: Let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be positive reals and $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ random variables. \begin{itemize} \item $X_n = o_p(a_n)$ if for all $\varepsilon > 0$, $\mathbb{P}\!\big(|X_n|/a_n > \varepsilon\big) \to 0$. \item $X_n = O_p(a_n)$ if for all $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $M > 0$ with $\limsup_n \mathbb{P}\!\big(|X_n|/a_n > M\big) \le \varepsilon$ (boundedness in probability of $X_n / a_n$). \end{itemize}
nodes.label: def:op_Op

nodes.name: $o_p$ and $O_p$ under scaling
nodes.statement: If $X_n = o_p(a_n)$ and $b_n / a_n \to c \in \mathbb{R}$, then $X_n = o_p(b_n)$ whenever $c \neq 0$; similarly for $O_p$. Moreover $o_p(a_n) + o_p(a_n) = o_p(a_n)$, $O_p(a_n) + O_p(a_n) = O_p(a_n)$, and $o_p(a_n) + O_p(a_n) = O_p(a_n)$.
nodes.label: lem:op_smul

nodes.statement: Direct from the definitions and a union bound.

nodes.name: $\aRTS$ family
nodes.statement: Let $K \ge 2$, $\alpha \in [0,1)$ and $m_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ (a burn-in parameter). A RAR procedure is an \emph{$\alpha$-Rebalancing Targeting Strategy} ($\alpha\text{RTS}$) if its allocation probabilities $p_{m+1} \in \Delta_K$ satisfy, for all $m \ge K m_0$, the \emph{throttling condition} \begin{equation} \forall k \in [K], \quad \frac{N_{m,k}}{m} > \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \ \Longrightarrow\ p_{m+1,k} \le \alpha\, \hat{\rho}_{m,k}. \end{equation} In words: whenever arm $k$ is currently over-sampled relative to its estimated target, the probability of selecting it next is throttled down to at most $\alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.label: def:aRTS

nodes.statement: The burn-in parameter $m_0$ is the number of initial samples of each arm that may be taken before adaptive randomization starts. It plays no role in the proofs; one may take $m_0 = 0$ when the regularization $\theta_0$ of the estimator is chosen appropriately.
nodes.label: rem:burnin

nodes.name: Distance-based design
nodes.statement: Given $\alpha \in [0,1)$, the \emph{distance-based} design sets, for $m \ge K m_0$ and $k \in [K]$, \[ p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\, \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + (1-\alpha)\frac{\delta_{m,k}}{\sum_{i=1}^K \delta_{m,i}}, \qquad \delta_{m,k} := \max\!\Big(0,\ \hat{\rho}_{m,k} - \frac{N_{m,k}}{m}\Big), \] with the convention that if $\delta_{m,j} = 0$ for all $j$, then $p_{m+1,j} = \hat{\rho}_{m,j}$ for all $j$.
nodes.label: def:distance_design

nodes.name: Distance-based is a valid probability vector
nodes.statement: For all $m \ge K m_0$, the vector $p_{m+1}$ of Definition~\ref{def:distance_design} lies in $\Delta_K$.
nodes.label: lem:distance_simplex

nodes.statement: Each coordinate is nonnegative, and $\sum_k p_{m+1,k} = \alpha \sum_k \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + (1-\alpha)\frac{\sum_k \delta_{m,k}}{\sum_i \delta_{m,i}} = \alpha + (1-\alpha) = 1$ when some $\delta_{m,i}>0$; in the degenerate case $p_{m+1}=\hat{\rho}_m \in \Delta_K$.

nodes.name: Distance-based is $\aRTS$
nodes.statement: The distance-based design satisfies the throttling condition \eqref{eq:throttle}, hence belongs to the $\alpha\text{RTS}$ family.
nodes.label: lem:distance_isARTS

nodes.statement: Membership in $\Delta_K$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:distance_simplex}. For the throttle: if $N_{m,k}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ then $\delta_{m,k} = 0$, so $p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k} \le \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$. \emph{Formalization.} The design is \texttt{AlphaRAR.distanceProb} (a probability-vector function of the history) and the algorithm \texttt{AlphaRAR.distanceAlgorithm}; \texttt{AlphaRAR.distanceProb\_ throttle} is the throttle inequality. The only subtlety is that the mixing normaliser $\sum_i \delta_{m,i}$ is positive whenever some arm is over-sampled: the signed deficits $N_{m,i}/m - \hat\rho_{m,i}$ sum to $0$ (\texttt{sum\_histProp}, \texttt{sum\_histTarget}), so an over-sampled arm forces an under-sampled one, giving $\delta_{m,j}>0$ for some $j$.

nodes.name: ERADE 2025 design
nodes.statement: Given $\alpha \in [0,1)$, the \emph{ERADE 2025} design of \cite{alkhnefr2025efficient} sets, for $m \ge K m_0$ and $k \in [K]$, \[ p_{m+1,k} = \begin{cases} \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k}, & N_{m,k}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,k},\\ \hat{\rho}_{m,k}, & N_{m,k}/m = \hat{\rho}_{m,k},\\ \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + (1-\alpha)\dfrac{\sum_{j\in S}\hat{\rho}_{m,j}}{|T|}, & N_{m,k}/m < \hat{\rho}_{m,k}, \end{cases} \] where $S = \{ j : N_{m,j}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,j}\}$ is the set of over-sampled arms and $T = \{ j : N_{m,j}/m < \hat{\rho}_{m,j}\}$ the set of under-sampled arms.
nodes.label: def:erade2025

nodes.name: ERADE 2025 is a valid probability vector
nodes.statement: For all $m \ge K m_0$, the vector $p_{m+1}$ of Definition~\ref{def:erade2025} lies in $\Delta_K$.
nodes.label: lem:erade2025_simplex

nodes.statement: Nonnegativity is clear. For the sum, the total mass removed from over-sampled arms is $\sum_{j\in S}(1-\alpha)\hat{\rho}_{m,j}$, which is exactly the mass added on the $|T|$ under-sampled arms, and arms with equality keep their target; using $\sum_k \hat{\rho}_{m,k} = 1$ gives $\sum_k p_{m+1,k} = 1$.

nodes.name: ERADE 2025 is $\aRTS$
nodes.statement: The ERADE 2025 design satisfies \eqref{eq:throttle}, hence belongs to the $\alpha\text{RTS}$ family.
nodes.label: lem:erade2025_isARTS

nodes.statement: Membership in $\Delta_K$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:erade2025_simplex}. For the throttle: if $N_{m,k}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ then $p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$. \emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.eradeProb}/\texttt{eradeAlgorithm} and \texttt{AlphaRAR.eradeProb\_throttle}. The simplex identity uses that the mass freed from the over-sampled arms, $\sum_{j\in S}(1-\alpha)\hat\rho_{m,j}$, is redistributed exactly over the $|T|$ under-sampled arms; the degenerate case $|T|=0$ forces $S=\varnothing$ by mass conservation (\texttt{sum\_histProp\_le}, \texttt{sum\_histTarget}) --- the proportions never total more than $1$, which also covers the empty history, where every count is $0$.

nodes.name: Interpolated D-Tracking
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \in [0,1)$, the \emph{Interpolated D-Tracking} rule sets, for $m \ge K m_0$ and $k \in [K]$, \[ p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\, \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + (1-\alpha)\,\mathbf{1}_{\{k = k^\star\}}, \qquad k^\star \in arg\,max_{a \in [K]} \big\{ m\hat{\rho}_{m,a} - N_{m,a} \big\}. \] The quantity $m\hat{\rho}_{m,a} - N_{m,a}$ is the deficit of arm $a$ relative to its target, so $k^\star$ is the most under-sampled arm.
nodes.label: def:d_tracking

nodes.name: Interpolated D-Tracking is a valid probability vector
nodes.statement: For all $m \ge K m_0$, $p_{m+1} \in \Delta_K$.
nodes.label: lem:d_tracking_simplex

nodes.statement: $\sum_k p_{m+1,k} = \alpha \sum_k \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + (1-\alpha) = 1$, and each coordinate is nonnegative.

nodes.name: Interpolated D-Tracking is $\aRTS$
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha \in [0,1)$, the Interpolated D-Tracking rule satisfies \eqref{eq:throttle}, hence belongs to the $\alpha\text{RTS}$ family.
nodes.label: lem:d_tracking_isARTS

nodes.statement: Membership in $\Delta_K$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:d_tracking_simplex}. If $N_{m,k}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ then $m\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - N_{m,k} < 0$. Since $\sum_a (m\hat{\rho}_{m,a} - N_{m,a}) = 0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:counts_sum}, the maximizing deficit is $\ge 0$, so $k \ne k^\star$ and $p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$. \emph{Formalization.} The favoured arm $k^\star=\arg\max_a(m\hat\rho_{m,a}-N_{m,a})$ is \texttt{argmax} of \texttt{AlphaRAR.dtDeficit} (LeanMachineLearning's measurable finite-tuple \texttt{argmax}, so the policy kernel is measurable without needing an order on the arms); the throttle is \texttt{AlphaRAR.dTrackingProb\_throttle}.

When $\alpha = 0$, the Interpolated D-Tracking rule becomes $p_{m+1,k} = \mathbf{1}_{\{k = k^\star\}}$, which is the D-Tracking rule of \cite{garivier2016optimal} (without its forced-exploration component, treated in Chapter~\ref{chap:forced}).
nodes.label: rem:d_tracking_zero

nodes.name: Conditional selection probability
nodes.statement: For $k \in [K]$ and $m \ge 1$, \[ p_{m,k} := \mathbb{E}[X_{m,k} \mid \mathcal{F}_{m-1}]. \] For a RAR procedure these coincide with the allocation probabilities: with the indexing convention of Definition~\ref{def:rar}, $p_{m,k}$ is the $k$-th component of the vector used to draw $X_m$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale
nodes.label: def:cond_prob

nodes.name: $p_{m,k}$ is the conditional probability
nodes.statement: $p_{m,k}$ is a \emph{version} of $\mathbb{E}[X_{m,k}\mid\mathcal{F}_{m-1}]$: it is $\mathcal{F}_{m-1}$-measurable, locally integrable, and has the same integral as $X_{m,k}$ over every $\mathcal{F}_{m-1}$-measurable set of finite measure. Anything with those three properties is a.s.\ equal to it. The content is the index: conditioning on $\mathcal{F}_m$ instead would return $X_{m,k}$ itself, the assignment being known by then, and $p_{m,k}$ would cease to be a probability of anything.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale
nodes.label: lem:cond_prob_unique

nodes.statement: Existence and a.s.\ uniqueness of the conditional expectation, the latter being the fact that a $\mathcal{F}_{m-1}$-measurable function is determined a.s.\ by its integrals over $\mathcal{F}_{m-1}$-sets.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale

nodes.name: Assignment martingale
nodes.statement: For $k \in [K]$ set $\Delta M_{m,k} := X_{m,k} - p_{m,k}$ and \[ M_{n,k} := \sum_{m=1}^n (X_{m,k} - p_{m,k}), \qquad M_n := (M_{n,1},\dots,M_{n,K}). \]
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale
nodes.label: def:M

nodes.name: $M$ is a martingale
nodes.statement: For each $k \in [K]$, $(M_{n,k})_{n\ge0}$ is an $(\mathcal{F}_n)$-martingale with $M_{0,k}=0$ and bounded increments $|\Delta M_{m,k}| \le 1$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale
nodes.label: lem:M_martingale

nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[\Delta M_{m,k}\mid\mathcal{F}_{m-1}] = \mathbb{E}[X_{m,k}\mid\mathcal{F}_{m-1}] - p_{m,k} = 0$ by Definition~\ref{def:cond_prob}, and $X_{m,k},p_{m,k}\in[0,1]$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale

nodes.name: $M$ is the unique compensator of the count
nodes.statement: $M_{\cdot,k}$ is the Doob martingale part of the count $N_{\cdot,k}$ against $(\mathcal{F}_{n-1})$: it is an $(\mathcal{F}_{n-1})$-martingale, $M_{0,k}=0$, and what it removes from the count — the accumulated selection probabilities $N_{\cdot,k}-M_{\cdot,k}$ — is predictable. Any process with those three properties is indistinguishable from it. Predictability is what makes the martingale property pin $M$ down: without it, adding any martingale null at $0$ would give another candidate.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale
nodes.label: lem:M_unique

nodes.statement: Existence is Lemma~\ref{lem:M_martingale} together with predictability of the Doob predictable part. For uniqueness, $N = M + (N-M)$ exhibits the count as a martingale plus a predictable process null at $0$, and that decomposition is unique up to null sets, one per time; the index set is countable, so the exceptional sets union to a null set.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale

nodes.name: The assignment martingale is $O_p(\sqrt n)$
nodes.statement: For each $k \in [K]$, $M_{n,k} = O_p(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale
nodes.label: lem:M_Op

nodes.statement: $M_{\cdot,k}$ is a martingale with $M_{0,k}=0$ and increments bounded by $1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:M_martingale}), so Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_bdd_incr_Op} applies with $c = 1$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale

nodes.name: Count decomposition
nodes.statement: For all $n\ge1$ and $k\in[K]$, $\displaystyle N_{n,k} = \sum_{m=1}^n p_{m,k} + M_{n,k}$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale
nodes.label: lem:count_decomp

nodes.statement: Sum the identity $X_{m,k} = p_{m,k} + \Delta M_{m,k}$ over $m \le n$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Conditional probabilities and the assignment martingale

nodes.name: Centered response martingale
nodes.statement: For $k \in [K]$ set $Y_{m,k} := \xi_{m,k} - \theta_k$ and \[ Q_{n,k} := \sum_{m=1}^n X_{m,k}\,(\xi_{m,k} - \theta_k) = \sum_{m=1}^n X_{m,k}\,Y_{m,k}, \qquad Q_n := (Q_{n,1}, \dots, Q_{n,K}). \]
nodes.label: def:Q

nodes.name: $Q$ is a martingale
nodes.statement: For each $k \in [K]$, if the responses are integrable then $(Q_{n,k})_{n\ge0}$ is a $(\mathcal{G}_n)$-martingale, where $\mathcal{G}_n := \mathcal{F}_{n-1}\vee\sigma(A_n)$ is the action-augmented filtration (\texttt{filtrationAction}); a fortiori it is an $(\mathcal{F}_n)$-martingale.
nodes.label: lem:Q_martingale

nodes.statement: Write $\Delta Q_{n,k} = X_{n,k}(\xi_{n,k} - \theta_k)$, where $X_{n,k}$ is the indicator that the assignment $A_n$ equals arm $k$. The natural filtration is the \emph{action-augmented} one $\mathcal{G}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n-1}\vee\sigma(A_n)$ (\texttt{filtrationAction}): the assignment $X_{n,k}$ is $\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable (the arm is known) while the response $\xi_{n,k}$ is not (it is revealed afterwards). Conditioning on $\mathcal{G}_n$, the response is drawn from the arm's reward kernel independently of the past given the arm, so its conditional mean is $\theta_k$; pulling out the $\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable factor $X_{n,k}$ gives $\mathbb{E}[\Delta Q_{n,k}\mid\mathcal{G}_n] = X_{n,k}(\theta_k-\theta_k)=0$, so $Q_{\cdot,k}$ is a $\mathcal{G}$-martingale. Since $Q_{n,k}$ is $\mathcal{F}_{n-1}\subseteq\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable, the tower property also gives $\mathbb{E}[\Delta Q_{n,k}\mid\mathcal{F}_{n-1}] = 0$, the paper's $\mathcal{F}$-martingale statement. This is formalized in the \texttt{LeanMachineLearning} algorithm--environment framework: the arm is the action and the response is the feedback of a stationary environment with per-arm reward kernel $\nu$, and $\theta_k = \int x\,\nu_k(dx)$ is the kernel mean. The conditional-mean computation is \texttt{condExp\_feedback} (which handles the first patient and the general step via the two conditional-distribution fields of the framework), and the filtration $\mathcal{G}$ is \texttt{filtrationAction}.

nodes.name: Conditional second moment of $\Delta Q$
nodes.statement: For each $k \in [K]$, conditioning on the action-augmented $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{G}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n-1}\vee\sigma(A_n)$ (\texttt{filtrationAction}), \[ \mathbb{E}\big[(\Delta Q_{n,k})^2 \mid \mathcal{G}_n\big] = X_{n,k}\, V_k, \] where $V_k = \mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}[\xi_{1,k}] = \int (x-\theta_k)^2\,\nu_k(dx)$ is the variance of arm $k$ (Mathlib's \texttt{variance}: \texttt{Var[id; ν k]}).
nodes.label: lem:Q_cond_second_moment

nodes.statement: Since $X_{n,k}$ is a $\{0,1\}$-indicator, $X_{n,k}^2 = X_{n,k}$ and hence $(\Delta Q_{n,k})^2 = X_{n,k}(\xi_{n,k}-\theta_k)^2$. The factor $X_{n,k}$ is $\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable, so it pulls out of the conditional expectation; by the same conditional-distribution computation as in Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_martingale} --- now applied to $g(x) = (x-\theta_k)^2$ (\texttt{condExp\_feedback\_comp}) --- the response's conditional second central moment given $\mathcal{G}_n$ is $\int (x-\theta_k)^2\,\nu_{A_n}(dx)$. On the event $\{A_n = k\}$ this integral equals $V_k$, while off it $X_{n,k}=0$; in either case the product is $X_{n,k} V_k$.

nodes.name: Quadratic variation of $Q$
nodes.statement: Under Condition~\textbf{A}, the predictable quadratic variation of $Q_{\cdot,k}$ is $\langle Q_{\cdot,k}\rangle_n = V_k N_{n,k}$: the process $Q_{\cdot,k}^2 - V_k N_{\cdot,k}$ is a martingale, with $V_k N_{\cdot,k}$ its predictable compensator.
nodes.label: lem:Q_quad_var

nodes.statement: Since $Q_{\cdot,k}$ is a martingale for the action-augmented filtration $\mathcal{G} = \texttt{filtrationAction}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_martingale}), the paper's $V_k N_{n,k}$ is the \emph{ordinary} predictable quadratic variation of $Q_{\cdot,k}$ for $\mathcal{G}$ (Definition~\ref{def:pred_qv}): its increment is $\mathbb{E}[(\Delta Q_{m+1,k})^2\mid\mathcal{G}_m] = V_k X_{m,k}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_cond_second_moment}), and summing over $m<n$ gives $V_k\sum_{m<n} X_{m,k} = V_k N_{n,k}$ --- the indicator survives the sum because the current arm $A_m$ is $\mathcal{G}_m$-measurable. That $Q^2-\langle Q\rangle$ is a martingale (for $\mathcal{G}$) is Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_mart}. The sole hypothesis is finite arm variance (Condition~\textbf{A}), formalized as $\xi_{\cdot,k}\in L^2$.

nodes.name: Second moment of $Q$
nodes.statement: Under Condition~\textbf{A}, for each $k \in [K]$, $\mathbb{E}[Q_{n,k}^2] = V_k\,\mathbb{E}[N_{n,k}]$.
nodes.label: lem:Q_second_moment

nodes.statement: The discrete Itô isometry (Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_second_moment}) gives $\mathbb{E}[Q_{n,k}^2] = \mathbb{E}[\langle Q_{\cdot,k}\rangle_n]$ for the martingale $Q_{\cdot,k}$ (which starts at $0$), and $\langle Q_{\cdot,k}\rangle_n = V_k N_{n,k}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_quad_var}; taking expectations, $\mathbb{E}[Q_{n,k}^2] = V_k\,\mathbb{E}[N_{n,k}]$.

nodes.name: Cross variation of $Q$
nodes.statement: For $k \ne j$, the cross variation vanishes: $\langle Q_{\cdot,k}, Q_{\cdot,j}\rangle_n = 0$. Equivalently, $Q_{\cdot,k}\,Q_{\cdot,j}$ is a martingale (for the action-augmented filtration $\mathcal{G}$).
nodes.label: lem:Q_cross_var

nodes.statement: The increments $\Delta Q_{\cdot,k}$ and $\Delta Q_{\cdot,j}$ are orthogonal --- indeed their product is \emph{identically} zero, since $X_{m,k}X_{m,j} = 0$ for $k \ne j$ (each patient is assigned to exactly one arm, \texttt{respMart\_increment\_mul\_eq\_zero}). Hence $Q_{\cdot,k}\,Q_{\cdot,j}$ is a martingale by Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_orthogonal} (\texttt{martingale\_mul}), so its predictable compensator --- the cross variation --- is $0$.

nodes.name: The response martingale is $O_p(\sqrt n)$
nodes.statement: For each $k \in [K]$, if the responses are square-integrable (Condition~\textbf{A}), then $Q_{n,k} = O_p(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.label: lem:Q_Op

nodes.statement: $Q_{\cdot,k}$ is a martingale (for the action-augmented filtration $\mathcal{G}$) with $Q_{0,k}=0$, and its increment second moments are bounded by the arm variance: taking expectations in Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_cond_second_moment} via the tower property, $\mathbb{E}[(\Delta Q_{n+1,k})^2] = \mathbb{E}[X_{n,k}\,V_k] = V_k\,\mathbb{P}(X_{n,k}=1) \le V_k$ (\texttt{integral\_respMart\_increment\_sq\_le}). So Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_Op} applies with $\sigma^2 = V_k$.

nodes.name: Estimator error via $Q$
nodes.statement: On $\{N_{m,k}\ge1\}$, the leading term of the estimator error is $\dfrac{1}{N_{m,k}}\sum_{j=1}^m X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} - \theta_k = \dfrac{Q_{m,k}}{N_{m,k}}$. Consequently, under the Bahadur representation (Definition~\ref{def:bahadur}), $\hat{\theta}_{m,k} - \theta_k = \dfrac{Q_{m,k}}{N_{m,k}} + o(N_{m,k}^{-1/2})$.
nodes.label: lem:theta_error_Q

nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{N_{m,k}}\sum_j X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k} - \theta_k = \frac{1}{N_{m,k}}\sum_j X_{j,k}(\xi_{j,k}-\theta_k) = \frac{Q_{m,k}}{N_{m,k}}$, using $\sum_j X_{j,k} = N_{m,k}$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary process $U$
nodes.statement: For a fixed $\alpha \in [0,1)$, $k \in [K]$ and $n \ge 0$ (with the $0$-indexed convention, patient $0$ first), \[ U_{n,k} := \sum_{m=0}^{n-1} \alpha\, \hat{\rho}_{m,k} + M_{n,k} - n\, \hat{\rho}_{n,k}. \] The leading sum runs over $m < n$, so it uses the plug-in targets of patients $0,\dots,n-1$.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time
nodes.label: def:U

nodes.name: Increment of $U$
nodes.statement: For all $n \ge 0$ and $k \in [K]$, \[ \Delta U_{n,k} = U_{n+1,k} - U_{n,k} = \alpha\, \hat{\rho}_{n,k} - p_{n,k} + \Delta\big(N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}\big), \] where we used $\Delta M_{n,k} = X_{n,k} - p_{n,k}$ and $\Delta N_{n,k} = X_{n,k}$. The selection probability $p_{n,k}$ is paired with the target $\hat\rho_{n,k}$ at the \emph{same} index, so the throttle discharged downstream is $p_{n,k} \le \alpha\hat\rho_{n,k}$ (patient $n$ is allocated using the target of patients $0,\dots,n-1$). The identity holds at $n=0$ too, since the $\alpha\hat\rho$ sum grows at every step.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time
nodes.label: lem:U_increment

nodes.statement: Direct computation from Definition~\ref{def:U}, expanding $M_{n+1,k} - M_{n,k} = X_{n,k} - p_{n,k}$ and telescoping.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time

nodes.name: Last under-sampling time
nodes.statement: For $k \in [K]$ and $n \ge 1$, the \emph{last under-sampling time} before $n$ is \[ \ell_{n,k} := \max\Big\{\, m \le n : \frac{N_{m,k}}{m} \le \hat{\rho}_{m,k} \,\Big\}. \] It is the last time up to $n$ at which arm $k$ is under-sampled (its proportion is at most its estimated target).
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time
nodes.label: def:hitting

nodes.name: Basic properties of the hitting time
nodes.statement: For each $k$, $(\ell_{n,k})_{n\ge1}$ is non-decreasing and $\ell_{n,k} \le n$.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time
nodes.label: lem:hitting_basic

nodes.statement: Immediate from the definition: enlarging $n$ enlarges the set over which the max is taken, and the max is bounded by $n$.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time

nodes.name: Sign at the hitting time
nodes.statement: For $m > \ell_{n,k}$ (and $m \le n$), $\frac{N_{m,k}}{m} > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$; in particular, for an $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design with $m \ge Km_0$, $p_{m+1,k} \le \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time
nodes.label: lem:hitting_sign

nodes.statement: By maximality of $\ell_{n,k}$, no $m$ with $\ell_{n,k} < m \le n$ satisfies $N_{m,k}/m \le \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$. The second statement is the throttling condition \eqref{eq:throttle}.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time

nodes.name: The hitting time is the last such time
nodes.statement: Three properties characterize $\ell_{n,k}$: it is $\le n$; no $m$ with $\ell_{n,k}<m\le n$ is under-sampled; and $\ell_{n,k}$ is itself under-sampled unless it is $0$. No other number has all three. The last clause is the empty-set convention of the Lean remark above, stated rather than left implicit — it is what gives $\ell_{n,k}$ a value when arm $k$ is never under-sampled up to $n$, and what keeps that value from being arbitrary.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time
nodes.label: lem:hitting_unique

nodes.statement: Existence is Lemmas~\ref{lem:hitting_basic} and~\ref{lem:hitting_sign} together with the fact that the maximum is attained whenever the set is nonempty. For uniqueness, of two candidates the smaller one's maximality rules the larger one out, which forces the larger to be $0$ and hence not larger after all.
nodes.section: 3.3 The auxiliary process \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} and the last hitting time

nodes.name: Bounded expectation gives $O_p$
nodes.statement: Let $(u_n)_{n\ge1}$ be positive reals and $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ real random variables. If there is $C > 0$ with $\mathbb{E}|X_n| \le C u_n$ for all $n$, then $X_n = O_p(u_n)$.
nodes.label: lem:expectation_to_O

nodes.statement: By Markov's inequality, $\mathbb{P}(|X_n| > M u_n) \le \mathbb{E}|X_n|/(M u_n) \le C/M$. Given $\varepsilon > 0$, take $M \ge C/\varepsilon$ to get $\mathbb{P}(|X_n| > M u_n) \le \varepsilon$ for all $n$, which is the definition of $X_n = O_p(u_n)$.

nodes.name: Bounded second moment gives $O_p$
nodes.statement: Let $(u_n)_{n\ge1}$ be positive reals and $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ real random variables. If there is $C \ge 0$ with $\mathbb{E}[X_n^2] \le C u_n^2$ for all $n$, then $X_n = O_p(u_n)$.
nodes.label: lem:sq_expectation_to_O

nodes.statement: By Chebyshev's inequality, $\mathbb{P}(|X_n| > M u_n) = \mathbb{P}(X_n^2 > M^2 u_n^2) \le \mathbb{E}[X_n^2]/(M^2 u_n^2) \le C/M^2$, which is $\le \varepsilon$ once $M \ge \sqrt{C/\varepsilon}$. Equivalently, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:expectation_to_O} to $X_n^2$ with rate $u_n^2$ to get $X_n^2 = O_p(u_n^2)$, then take square roots.

nodes.name: Doob $L^2$ maximal bound for martingale differences
nodes.statement: Let $\{M_n, \mathcal{F}_n\}$ be a martingale with $\mathbb{E}|\Delta M_n|^2 \le C_0$ for all $n$. Then for any integer $L$, \[ \mathbb{E}\Big[\max_{1 \le m \le L} |M_n - M_{n-m}|\Big] \le 4\sqrt{C_0 L}. \]
nodes.label: lem:mart_maximal

nodes.statement: Fix $n$ and set $S_k := M_{n-L+k} - M_{n-L}$ for $0 \le k \le L$, a martingale for the shifted filtration $\mathcal{G}_k := \mathcal{F}_{n-L+k}$. First, $\max_{1\le m\le L}|M_n - M_{n-m}| \le 2\max_{1\le k\le L}|S_k|$ by the triangle inequality. Since $\{S_k^2\}$ is a submartingale, Doob's maximal inequality gives $\mathbb{P}(\max_k |S_k| \ge x) \le \mathbb{E}[S_L^2]/x^2$. Orthogonality of martingale increments yields $\mathbb{E}[S_L^2] = \sum_{k=1}^L \mathbb{E}|\Delta M_{n-L+k}|^2 \le L C_0$. Combining, $\mathbb{P}(\max_m |M_n - M_{n-m}| \ge x) \le 4 L C_0 / x^2$, and integrating the tail, $\mathbb{E}[\max_m |M_n-M_{n-m}|] \le \int_0^{2\sqrt{LC_0}} 1\,dx + 4\int_{2\sqrt{LC_0}}^\infty \frac{LC_0}{x^2}\,dx = 4\sqrt{LC_0}$. \emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal} states the equivalent $\int^-$ (lintegral) bound $\int^- \max_{m\le L}|M_n - M_{n-m}| \le 4\sqrt{C_0 L}$ (the $m=0$ term is $0$, so $\max_{m\le L}=\max_{1\le m\le L}$), which is the form consumed downstream via \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_lintegral\_le}. The three substantive ingredients are separate reusable lemmas filling a Mathlib gap: the shifted martingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.martingale\_shift}, Doob's $L^2$ submartingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.submartingale\_sq}, and the $L^2$ maximal inequality \texttt{AlphaRAR.lintegral\_sup'\_abs\_le\_two\_mul\_sqrt} (whose analytic core is the tail-to-$L^1$ lemma \texttt{MeasureTheory.lintegral\_le\_two\_mul\_sqrt\_of\_meas\_ge\_le}).

nodes.name: Dyadic maximal bound
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal}, for any $L$ with $0 < L \le n$, \[ \mathbb{E}\Big[\max_{L \le m \le n} \frac{|M_n - M_{n-m}|}{m}\Big] \le 32\sqrt{\frac{C_0}{L}}. \]
nodes.label: lem:mart_maximal_dyadic

nodes.statement: Split the range $[L,n]$ into dyadic blocks $2^{j-1} \le m < 2^j$. On such a block $\frac1m \le \frac{2}{2^j}$, so $\mathbb{E}[\max_{L\le m\le n}\frac{|M_n-M_{n-m}|}{m}] \le \sum_{j \ge \log_2 L} \frac{2}{2^j}\, \mathbb{E}[\max_{m<2^j}|M_n-M_{n-m}|] \le \sum_{j\ge\log_2 L} \frac{2}{2^j}\, 4\sqrt{C_0 2^j} = 8\sqrt{C_0}\sum_{j\ge\log_2 L} 2^{-j/2}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal}. The geometric sum $\sum_{j\ge\log_2 L} 2^{-j/2} = (2+\sqrt2)\,2^{-\lceil\log_2 L\rceil/2} \le 4/\sqrt L$ (using $\tfrac1{1-1/\sqrt2} = 2+\sqrt2 \le 4$ and $2^{\lceil\log_2 L\rceil}\ge L$), giving the bound $32\sqrt{C_0/L}$. \emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_dyadic} states the equivalent $\int^-$ (lintegral) bound $\int^- \max_{L\le m\le n}\frac{|M_n-M_{n-m}|}{m} \le 32\sqrt{C_0/L}$ (the constant $32 = 8(2+\sqrt2)$ rounded up, which suffices for the downstream $o_p$; the exact constant is immaterial). The dyadic index of $m$ is $\lfloor\log_2 m\rfloor+1$ (\texttt{Nat.log}), the per-scale bound is Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} applied at $L' = \min(2^j-1,n)$, and the geometric series is bounded via \texttt{geom\_sum\_eq} with ratio $1/\sqrt2 \le 3/4$.

nodes.name: Vector maximal bounds
nodes.statement: Let $(M_{\cdot,k})_{k\in[K]}$ be a finite family of martingales, each satisfying the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} with the same bound $C_0$. Then, for $L\le n$, \[ \mathbb{E}\Big[\max_{m\le L}\|M_n - M_{n-m}\|\Big] \le 4K\sqrt{C_0 L}, \] and, for $0<L\le n$, \[ \mathbb{E}\Big[\max_{L\le m\le n}\frac{\|M_n - M_{n-m}\|}{m}\Big] \le 32K\sqrt{\tfrac{C_0}{L}}, \] where $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{R}^K$.
nodes.label: lem:mart_maximal_pi

nodes.statement: By the $\ell^2\le\ell^1$ inequality $\|v\| = \sqrt{\sum_k v_k^2}\le\sum_k|v_k|$, the running maximum of the norm is bounded by $\sum_k$ of the coordinatewise running maxima (maximum of a sum $\le$ sum of maxima), and each coordinate is controlled by Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} (resp.\ Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_dyadic}). Summing the $K$ scalar bounds gives the factor $K$. \emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_pi} and \texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_dyadic\_pi} state the $\int^-$ forms with the norm written as $\sqrt{\sum_k(M_{n,k}-M_{n-m,k})^2}$. The coordinate interchange uses \texttt{Finset.sup'\_le} and \texttt{Finset.le\_sup'}; the $\ell^2\le\ell^1$ step is \texttt{sum\_sq\_le\_sq\_sum\_of\_nonneg}; integration term-by-term is \texttt{lintegral\_finsetSum}.

nodes.name: Increment control from maximal bounds
nodes.statement: For any sequence $(Q_n)_{n\ge0}$ in a normed space, any $\ell$ with $0 \le \ell \le n$ and any $1 \le L < n$, \[ \|Q_n - Q_\ell\| \le (n - \ell)\max_{L \le m \le n}\frac{\|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|}{m} + \max_{m < L}\|Q_n - Q_{n-m}\|. \]
nodes.label: lem:increment_control

nodes.statement: Let $d := n - \ell$. If $d < L$, then $\|Q_n - Q_\ell\| = \|Q_n - Q_{n-d}\| \le \max_{m<L}\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|$. If $d \ge L$, then $\|Q_n - Q_\ell\| = d\cdot \frac{\|Q_n-Q_{n-d}\|}{d} \le (n-\ell)\max_{L\le m\le n}\frac{\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|}{m}$. Taking the larger of the two bounds proves the claim.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov-type inequality for martingales
nodes.statement: Let $\{X_n\}$ be a square-integrable martingale with $\mathbb{E}[X_1] = 0$. Then for $\lambda > 0$, \[ \mathbb{P}\Big(\max_{1\le i\le n} X_i \ge \lambda\Big) \le \frac{\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(X_n)}{\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(X_n) + \lambda^2}. \]
nodes.label: lem:chebyshev_mart

nodes.statement: For $\alpha > 0$, $\{\max_k X_k \ge \lambda\} \subseteq \{\max_k (X_k+\alpha)^2 \ge (\lambda+\alpha)^2\}$. As $\{(X_k+\alpha)^2\}$ is a submartingale, Doob's inequality gives $\mathbb{P}(\max_k(X_k+\alpha)^2 \ge (\lambda+\alpha)^2) \le \frac{\mathbb{E}[(X_n+\alpha)^2]}{(\lambda+\alpha)^2} = \frac{\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(X_n)+\alpha^2}{(\lambda+\alpha)^2}$. Optimizing at $\alpha = \mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(X_n)/\lambda$ gives $\frac{\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(X_n)}{\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(X_n)+\lambda^2}$.

nodes.name: Martingale is $O_p(\sqrt n)$
nodes.statement: Let $\{X_n\}$ be a square-integrable martingale with $X_0 = 0$ and increment second moments bounded, $\mathbb{E}[(\Delta X_{n+1})^2] \le \sigma^2$ (in particular stationary increment variances $\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(X_n) = n\sigma^2$). Then $X_n = O_p(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.label: cor:mart_Op

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_sq_growth}, $\mathbb{E}[X_n^2] \le \sigma^2 n$. Chebyshev's inequality (Lemma~\ref{lem:sq_expectation_to_O}) with rate $u_n = \sqrt n$ then gives $X_n = O_p(\sqrt n)$: $\mathbb{P}(|X_n| > M\sqrt n) \le \mathbb{E}[X_n^2]/(M^2 n) \le \sigma^2/M^2 \le \varepsilon$ for $M$ large, uniformly in $n$.

nodes.name: Bounded-increment martingale is $O_p(\sqrt n)$
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a martingale with $M_0 = 0$ whose increments are bounded, $|\Delta M_{n+1}| \le c$ a.s.\ for all $n$. Then $M_n = O_p(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.label: lem:mart_bdd_incr_Op

nodes.statement: Bounded increments give square-integrability of $M_n$ (indeed $|M_n| \le cn$ a.s.) and $\mathbb{E}[(\Delta M_{n+1})^2] \le c^2$, so Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_Op} applies with $\sigma^2 = c^2\,\mathbb{P}(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Variance equals inverse Fisher information
nodes.statement: For a regular one-parameter exponential family with density $f(y\mid\eta) = \exp\{\eta y - A(\eta)\}h(y)$, if the parameter of interest $\theta_k = A'(\eta_k)$ is the mean parameter and $\xi_{1,k} = Y$, then $\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(\xi_{1,k}) = I_k(\theta_k)^{-1}$, where $I_k$ is the Fisher information for one observation.
nodes.label: prop:exp_fam

nodes.statement: For the natural family, $\mathbb{E}_\eta[Y] = A'(\eta)$ and $\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}_\eta(Y) = A''(\eta)$. With $\theta_k = A'(\eta_k)$ one has $\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(\xi_{1,k}) = A''(\eta_k)$. By the reparameterization formula for Fisher information, $I_k(\theta_k) = I_{\eta_k}(\eta_k)\big(\frac{d\eta_k}{d\theta_k}\big)^2 = A''(\eta_k)\big(\frac{1}{A''(\eta_k)}\big)^2 = \frac{1}{A''(\eta_k)}$, so $\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(\xi_{1,k}) = I_k(\theta_k)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Positive-part convergence
nodes.statement: Let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a non-decreasing sequence with $a_n \le n$, let $\alpha, v \in [0,1]$, and let $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ be real with $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{X_n}{n} = -\alpha v$. Then for any real sequence $\varepsilon_n$ with $\limsup_n \varepsilon_n \le 0$, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty}\Big(\varepsilon_n + \frac{X_n - X_{a_n}}{n}\Big)^+ = 0. \]
nodes.label: lem:convergence

nodes.statement: If $(a_n)$ is bounded, it is eventually constant, so $X_{a_n}/n \to 0$ and $\varepsilon_n + \frac{X_n - X_{a_n}}{n} \to -\alpha v \le 0$, whence the positive part tends to $0$. If $a_n \to \infty$, then $X_{a_n}/a_n \to -\alpha v$; for $\varepsilon>0$ and $n$ large, $-\frac{X_{a_n}}{n} \le (\varepsilon + \alpha v)\frac{a_n}{n} \le \varepsilon + \alpha v$ (using $a_n \le n$), so $\varepsilon_n + \frac{X_n - X_{a_n}}{n} \le \varepsilon_n + \frac{X_n}{n} + \varepsilon + \alpha v$. Since $\frac{X_n}{n} + \alpha v \to 0$ and $\limsup \varepsilon_n \le 0$, the limsup of the left side is $\le \varepsilon$; as $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary the positive part tends to $0$.

nodes.name: Generic condition set
nodes.statement: Let $(\ell_{n,k})_{n\ge1, k\in[K]}$ be integer-valued random variables. We say that a RAR procedure \emph{satisfies the generic conditions with $\ell$} if: \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] for all $k$, $(\ell_{n,k})_n$ is non-decreasing and $\ell_{n,k}\le n$; \item[(ii)] for all $k,n$, \begin{equation} N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \le 1 + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}; \end{equation} \item[(iii)] for all $k,n$, \begin{equation} N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} = o(\sqrt n) \quad\text{a.s.} \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:generic_cond

nodes.name: Generic conditions imply the main theorems
nodes.statement: Suppose a RAR procedure satisfies the generic conditions with some $\ell$, and that Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B} hold. Then the conclusions of the strong consistency theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}) and of the asymptotic normality theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:normality}) hold. (The Lean statement \texttt{consistency\_of\_generic\_ae} formalizes the strong-consistency direction: the generic conditions and the plug-in-target limit imply $N_{n,k}/n \to u_k$ a.s.\ for every arm; the asymptotic-normality direction is not yet formalized.)
nodes.label: thm:generic_main

nodes.statement: This is the content of Chapters~\ref{chap:consistency} and \ref{chap:normality}: those chapters derive Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} and Theorem~\ref{thm:normality} using only the generic conditions of Definition~\ref{def:generic_cond} (together with Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}), never the specific form of the design.

nodes.name: Telescoping identity for $U$
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design and any $\ell_{n,k} \le n$, \[ N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} = N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}}^{n-1}\big(p_{m,k} - \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}\big) + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}. \]
nodes.label: lem:U_telescope

nodes.statement: Summing the increment identity of Lemma~\ref{lem:U_increment} from $m = \ell_{n,k}$ to $n-1$ gives $U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} = \sum_{m=\ell_{n,k}}^{n-1} (\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - p_{m,k}) + (N_{n,k}-n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}) - (N_{\ell_{n,k},k}-\ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k})$. Rearranging yields the claim.

nodes.name: Key inequality for $\aRTS$
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design, inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq} holds with the last under-sampling time of Definition~\ref{def:hitting}: \[ N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \le 1 + N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} + U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k}. \]
nodes.label: lem:preliminary_ineq

nodes.statement: In Lemma~\ref{lem:U_telescope}, each summand $p_{m,k} - \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ with $\ell_{n,k} < m \le n-1$ is $\le 0$: indeed $m > \ell_{n,k}$ so arm $k$ is over-sampled at time $m$ and the throttling condition (Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting_sign}) gives $p_{m,k} \le \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$. Dropping this nonpositive sum and bounding the single leftover boundary term $p_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le 1$ gives the inequality.

nodes.name: Smallness at the hitting time for $\aRTS$
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design, \eqref{eq:generic_small} holds: $N_{\ell_{n,k},k} - \ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le Km_0 = o(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.label: lem:preliminary_small

nodes.statement: If $\ell_{n,k} \ge Km_0+1$, then by definition of the hitting time $N_{\ell_{n,k},k}/\ell_{n,k} \le \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k}$, so the difference is $\le 0$. If $\ell_{n,k} < Km_0+1$, then $N_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le \ell_{n,k} \le Km_0$, so the difference is $\le Km_0$. Either way it is bounded by the constant $Km_0$, which is $o(\sqrt n)$.

nodes.name: $\aRTS$ satisfies the generic conditions
nodes.statement: Every $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design satisfies the generic conditions (Definition~\ref{def:generic_cond}) with $\ell_{n,k}$ the last under-sampling time of Definition~\ref{def:hitting}.
nodes.label: prop:aRTS_generic

nodes.statement: Condition (i) is Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting_basic}, condition (ii) is Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_ineq}, and condition (iii) is Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_small}. (The Lean lemmas \texttt{generic\_ineq\_of\_hitting} and \texttt{generic\_small\_of\_hitting} package Lemmas~\ref{lem:preliminary_ineq}--\ref{lem:preliminary_small} at the last under-sampling time $\ell_{n,k}$ into the operational forms \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}--\eqref{eq:generic_small}, given the $\alpha\text{RTS}$ throttle $\neg P_m \Rightarrow p_{m}\le\alpha\hat\rho_m$ (patient $m$ throttled by the target at the same index $m$). A single boundary summand $p_{\ell,k}-\alpha\hat\rho_{\ell,k}$ is uncontrolled by the throttle, so the constant in \eqref{eq:generic_ineq} is $1$. No lower bound on $\ell_{n,k}$ is needed: the telescoping identity holds at $\ell_{n,k}=0$ as well (the $\alpha\hat\rho$ sum of $U$ grows at every step), so the $0$-indexed edge case is automatic. The remaining step is to verify that a concrete $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design's selection probabilities satisfy the throttle — this is Definition~\ref{def:aRTS_alg} and Corollary~\ref{cor:aRTS_alg_consistency}.)

nodes.name: Strong consistency of the \texorpdfstring{$\aRTS$}{aRTS} proportions
nodes.statement: Consider an $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design driven by an algorithm–environment sequence under a stationary environment, with $Y_n\in L^2$ (Condition~\textbf{A}) and a continuous simplex-valued target map $\rho$. If the design's selection probabilities satisfy the throttle $\neg P_{m,k}\Rightarrow p_{m,k}\le\alpha\hat\rho_{m,k}$ a.s., then almost surely there is a common limit vector $v$ with $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ and $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to v_k$ for every arm $k$.
nodes.label: cor:aRTS_consistency

nodes.statement: Instantiate Theorem~\ref{thm:generic_main} with the assignment indicators $Y_{n,k}=\mathbf 1\{A_n=k\}$, the selection probabilities $p_{n,k}=P[\mathbf 1\{A_n=k\}\mid\mathcal{F}_{n-1}]$, the plug-in target $\hat\rho_{n,k}=\rho(\hat{\Theta}_n)_k$, and $\ell_{n,k}$ the last under-sampling time. The generic conditions are discharged by Proposition~\ref{prop:aRTS_generic} (the throttle is the stated design hypothesis); the vanishing normalized assignment martingale $M_{n,k}/n\to0$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:M_lln}, and the plug-in-target convergence $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to v_k$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges}. The common limit $v_k$ is that of $\hat\rho_{\cdot,k}$.

nodes.name: $\aRTS$ algorithm
nodes.statement: An algorithm chooses the action of patient $n$ from a history $h$ of the $n$ completed rounds (patients $0,\dots,n-1$) via a Markov kernel; the probability it assigns to arm $k$ is $\mathrm{policy}_n(h)(\{k\})$. The algorithm is an \emph{$\alpha$-throttled $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design} with offsets $\Theta_0$ and target map $\rho$ if its policy throttles every over-sampled arm: for every history $h$ and arm $k$, if $N_{n,k}(h) > n\,\hat\rho_k(h)$ then $\mathrm{policy}_n(h)(\{k\}) \le \alpha\,\hat\rho_k(h)$, where the count $N(h)$ and target $\hat\rho(h)=\rho(\hat{\Theta}(h))$ are computed from $h$. At $n=0$ the condition is vacuous, since $N_{0,k}=0$.
nodes.section: 5.3 The \texorpdfstring{$\aRTS$}{aRTS} family as a property of an algorithm
nodes.label: def:aRTS_alg

nodes.name: Consistency of an $\aRTS$ algorithm
nodes.statement: If the driving algorithm is an $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design (Definition~\ref{def:aRTS_alg}), under the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:aRTS_consistency}, then almost surely $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ and $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to v_k$ for every arm $k$. The companion \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_pullCount\_div\_ae\_tendsto} restates the proportion limit $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ with the pull count $N_{n,k}=\texttt{pullCount}$, the vocabulary in which the loglog estimator rate (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL}, \texttt{abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_loglog\_of\_proportion}) consumes it; only the strict positivity $v_k>0$ is then still required to apply that rate.
nodes.section: 5.3 The \texorpdfstring{$\aRTS$}{aRTS} family as a property of an algorithm
nodes.label: cor:aRTS_alg_consistency

nodes.statement: The policy-level throttle discharges the process-level throttle hypothesis of Corollary~\ref{cor:aRTS_consistency}. The link is that the selection probability $p_{n+1,k}=P[\mathbf 1\{A_{n+1}=k\}\mid\mathcal{F}_n]$ equals $\mathrm{policy}_{n+1}(\text{history}_{n+1})(\{k\})$ almost surely — a conditional expectation computed from the algorithm's conditional distribution of the next action given the history (\texttt{HasCondDistrib.condExp\_comp\_eq}) — and the history-level count and target agree with the process count $N_{n+1,k}$ and target $\hat\rho_{n+1,k}$.
nodes.section: 5.3 The \texorpdfstring{$\aRTS$}{aRTS} family as a property of an algorithm

nodes.name: SLLN for the response martingale
nodes.statement: For each arm $k$, on the event $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ the bracket-normalized response martingale vanishes: $\dfrac{Q_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}}\to 0$ a.s.
nodes.label: lem:respMart_div_count_slln

nodes.statement: The response martingale $Q_{\cdot,k}$ has predictable quadratic variation $\langle Q_k\rangle_n = V_k N_{n,k}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_quad_var}). If $V_k>0$, then on $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ the bracket $\langle Q_k\rangle_n = V_k N_{n,k}\to\infty$, so the bracket-normalized strong law (Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_slln_bracket}) gives $Q_{n,k}/\langle Q_k\rangle_n\to0$, whence $Q_{n,k}/N_{n,k} = V_k\,(Q_{n,k}/\langle Q_k\rangle_n)\to0$. If $V_k=0$, then $\mathbb{E}[Q_{n,k}^2] = V_k\,\mathbb{E}[N_{n,k}] = 0$, so $Q_{n,k}=0$ a.s.\ for every $n$ and the ratio is identically $0$.

nodes.name: Estimator limit on $\{N\to\infty\}$
nodes.statement: For each arm $k$, on the event $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ the estimator converges a.s.\ to the arm mean: $\hat\theta_{n,k}\to\theta_k$.
nodes.label: lem:theta_limit_infinite

nodes.statement: By the exact error identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}), $\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k = (Q_{n,k}+(\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k))/(N_{n,k}+1)$. On $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ the constant offset is $O(N_{n,k}^{-1})\to0$, while $\frac{Q_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}+1} = \frac{Q_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}}\cdot\frac{N_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}+1}\to0\cdot1=0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:respMart_div_count_slln}. Hence $\hat\theta_{n,k}\to\theta_k$.

nodes.name: Estimator eventually constant on $\{\sup_n N<\infty\}$
nodes.statement: For each arm $k$ and each realization, if $N_{n,k}\not\to\infty$ then $\hat\theta_{n,k}$ is eventually constant, and in particular converges.
nodes.label: lem:theta_limit_finite

nodes.statement: The count $N_{\cdot,k}$ is a nondecreasing $\mathbb{N}$-valued sequence, so $N_{n,k}\not\to\infty$ forces it to be bounded, hence eventually constant at its supremum $N_{N_0,k}$. For $n\ge N_0$ no further patient is assigned to arm $k$, so both the numerator $\sum_{j<n}X_{j,k}\xi_{j,k}$ and the denominator $N_{n,k}+1$ of $\hat\theta_{n,k}$ are frozen; hence $\hat\theta_{n,k}$ is eventually constant.

nodes.name: The sequential estimator converges a.s.
nodes.statement: For each arm $k$, the estimator $\hat\theta_{n,k}$ converges a.s.: to $\theta_k$ on $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ and to an eventually-attained value on $\{\sup_n N_{n,k}<\infty\}$.
nodes.label: lem:theta_converges

nodes.statement: The alternative $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ versus $\sup_n N_{n,k}<\infty$ is exhaustive (as $N_{n,k}$ is monotone in $n$); branch~1 is Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_infinite} and branch~2 is Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_finite}.

nodes.name: Dichotomy for the estimator limit
nodes.statement: Under Condition~\textbf{A}, for each $k$ the estimator $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}$ converges a.s.\ to a limit in $I_k$: on $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ it converges to $\theta_k$ by the strong law of large numbers; on $\{\sup_n N_{n,k} < \infty\}$ it is eventually constant and its limit lies in $V_k^{\mathrm{att}}$.
nodes.label: lem:theta_limit_dichotomy

nodes.statement: On $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$, the estimator converges a.s.\ to $\theta_k$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_infinite} (the martingale strong law applied to $Q_{\cdot,k}$). On $\{\sup_n N_{n,k}<\infty\}$, only finitely many responses on arm $k$ are ever observed, so $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}$ is eventually constant with a value in $V_k^{\mathrm{att}}$. \emph{Formalization} (\texttt{AlphaRAR.estimator\_limit\_mem\_attainableSet}). With the closure form of $I_k$ (Definition~\ref{def:attainable}) the case split is unnecessary: \emph{any} pointwise limit of $\hat{\theta}_{\cdot,k}$ is a limit of values in the range of the estimator, hence lies in the closure of that range, i.e.\ in $I_k$ (Mathlib's \texttt{mem\_closure\_of\_tendsto}).

nodes.name: The estimator vector converges a.s.
nodes.statement: With finitely many arms, the per-arm a.s.\ limits of Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_converges} combine into a single a.s.\ limit vector: almost surely there is $z\in\mathbb{R}^K$ with $\hat{\Theta}_n = (\hat\theta_{n,1},\dots,\hat\theta_{n,K}) \to z$.
nodes.label: lem:theta_converges_vec

nodes.statement: Each component converges a.s.\ by Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_converges}; intersecting the finitely many almost-sure events and choosing the (unique) limits componentwise gives a single a.s.\ event on which the whole vector converges.

nodes.name: Convergence of $\estTarget$ by continuity
nodes.statement: For any continuous target map $\rho$, the plug-in target $\hat{\rho}_n = \rho(\hat{\Theta}_n)$ converges a.s.: almost surely there is $u\in\mathbb{R}^K$ with $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$ for every $k$, where $u = \rho(z)$ and $z$ is the a.s.\ limit of $\hat{\Theta}_n$.
nodes.label: lem:rho_converges_cont

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_converges_vec}, $\hat{\Theta}_n \to z$ a.s.\ (in the product topology of $\mathbb{R}^K$). Continuity of $\rho$ transports this to $\hat{\rho}_n = \rho(\hat{\Theta}_n) \to \rho(z) =: u$, and taking components gives $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$.

nodes.name: Non-sparse limit of $\estTarget$
nodes.statement: Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B} there is a random $u \in (0,1)^K$ with $\hat{\rho}_n \to u$ a.s. Concretely $u = \rho(z)$ where $z\in I_1\times\dots\times I_K$ is the a.s.\ limit of $\hat{\Theta}_n$.
nodes.label: lem:rho_converges

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges_cont} (with $\rho$ continuous on $\mathcal{H}$ by Condition~\textbf{B}) and Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_dichotomy}, $\hat{\Theta}_n \to z$ a.s.\ with $z \in I_1\times\dots\times I_K$. By Condition~\textbf{B}, $\rho$ is continuous on the open set $\mathcal{H} \supseteq I_1\times\dots\times I_K$ and maps $I_1\times\dots\times I_K$ into $(0,1)^K$; hence $\hat{\rho}_n = \rho(\hat{\Theta}_n) \to \rho(z) =: u \in (0,1)^K$. \emph{Formalization} (\texttt{AlphaRAR.rho\_converges\_pos}). Condition~\textbf{B}'s non-sparsity enters as the hypothesis \texttt{hTpos}: $\rho$ maps the product of the attainable sets (Definition~\ref{def:attainable}) into the positive orthant. With $z$ the a.s.\ estimator-vector limit (\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_pi}), each $z_k\in I_k$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_dichotomy}), so \texttt{hTpos} gives $u_k=\rho(z)_k>0$ while continuity of $\rho$ gives $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$. The formalized conclusion is the positivity $u_k>0$ (the non-sparsity used downstream in Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_consistent}); the matching upper bound $u_k<1$ is the immediate consequence of the simplex constraint $\sum_k\rho(z)_k=1$.

nodes.name: LLN for the assignment martingale
nodes.statement: $M_{n,k} = o(n)$ a.s.\ for each $k$.
nodes.label: lem:M_lln

nodes.statement: $(M_{n,k})$ is a martingale with bounded increments $|\Delta M_{m,k}|\le1$, so its increments have summable normalized variances $\sum_m \frac{\mathbb{V}\mathrm{ar}(\Delta M_{m,k})}{m^2}<\infty$; the strong law of large numbers for martingales gives $M_{n,k}/n \to 0$ a.s.

nodes.name: Limit of $U/n$
nodes.statement: Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for each $k$, $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{U_{n,k}}{n} = -(1-\alpha)\,u_k$ a.s., where $u$ is the limit from Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges}. (The formalized statement \texttt{auxU\_div\_tendsto} is the deterministic core: for real sequences with $\rho_n\to u$ and $M_n/n\to0$, one has $U_n/n\to-(1-\alpha)u$; the a.s.\ statement is the pathwise application with the a.s.\ limits from Lemmas~\ref{lem:M_lln} and~\ref{lem:rho_converges}.)
nodes.label: lem:U_over_n

nodes.statement: From Definition~\ref{def:U}, $\frac{U_{n,k}}{n} = \frac{\alpha}{n}\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} + \frac{M_{n,k}}{n}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:M_lln} the last term is $o(1)$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges} $\hat{\rho}_{n,k}\to u_k$, and by Cesàro $\frac1n\sum_{m<n}\hat{\rho}_{m,k}\to u_k$. Hence $\frac{U_{n,k}}{n} \to \alpha u_k - u_k = -(1-\alpha)u_k$.

nodes.name: Positive part vanishes
nodes.statement: Under the generic conditions and Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for each $k$, $\big(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}\big)^+ \to 0$ a.s. (The formalized statement \texttt{pos\_part\_vanishes} is the pathwise core: it takes as hypotheses the plug-in convergence $\rho_n\to u$ (\ref{lem:rho_converges}), the vanishing $M_n/n\to0$ (\ref{lem:M_lln}), and the two generic conditions \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}--\eqref{eq:generic_small} in operational form.)
nodes.label: lem:pos_part_vanishes

nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:convergence} with $X_n := U_{n,k}$, $a_n := \ell_{n,k}$ (non-decreasing, $\le n$ by the generic conditions), and $\varepsilon_n := \frac1n + \frac{N_{\ell_{n,k},k}-\ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n}$, which satisfies $\limsup\varepsilon_n \le 0$ by \eqref{eq:generic_small}. Since $\frac{U_{n,k}}{n}\to -(1-\alpha)u_k$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:U_over_n}), the lemma yields $\big(\varepsilon_n + \frac{U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n}\big)^+ \to 0$. Combined with the generic inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}, which bounds $\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k}$ by that quantity, we get $\big(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k}\big)^+\to0$.

nodes.name: Negative part vanishes
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses, for each $k$, $\big(\hat{\rho}_{n,k} - \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\big)^+ \to 0$ a.s.
nodes.label: lem:neg_part_vanishes

nodes.statement: Using $\sum_j N_{n,j}/n = 1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:counts_sum}) and $\sum_j \hat{\rho}_{n,j} = 1$, $\big(\hat{\rho}_{n,k} - \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\big)^+ = \big(\sum_{j\ne k}(\frac{N_{n,j}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,j})\big)^+ \le \sum_{j\ne k}\big(\frac{N_{n,j}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,j}\big)^+ \to 0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:pos_part_vanishes}.

nodes.name: Proportions match the plug-in target
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses, for each $k$, $\frac{N_{n,k}}{n} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k} \to 0$ and $\frac{N_{n,k}}{n} \to u_k \in (0,1)$ a.s. (The formalized statement \texttt{match\_proportion} delivers $\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\to u_k$ from the two vanishing positive parts and $\hat{\rho}_{n,k}\to u_k$.)
nodes.label: lem:match

nodes.statement: The absolute value $|\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k}|$ is the sum of the two positive parts, both tending to $0$ by Lemmas~\ref{lem:pos_part_vanishes}--\ref{lem:neg_part_vanishes}. Since $\hat{\rho}_{n,k}\to u_k$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges}), also $\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\to u_k$.

nodes.name: All arms sampled infinitely often
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses, $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ a.s.\ for every $k$.
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency
nodes.label: lem:all_arms_infinite

nodes.statement: Since $\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\to u_k > 0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:match}), $N_{n,k}\sim u_k n \to\infty$.
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency

nodes.name: A.s. consistency of the proportions
nodes.statement: Given the a.s.\ vanishing positive gaps for every arm (Lemma~\ref{lem:pos_part_vanishes}) and the plug-in-target limits $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges_cont}), together with the simplex constraints ($\sum_k X_{j,k}=1$ and $\sum_k\hat\rho_{n,k}=1$), the proportions converge a.s.\ to the target: $N_{n,k}/n \to u_k$ for all arms $k$ simultaneously.
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency
nodes.label: lem:consistency_matching

nodes.statement: For each arm the negative gap vanishes by Lemma~\ref{lem:neg_part_vanishes}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:match} then yields $N_{n,k}/n\to u_k$; intersecting the finitely many a.s.\ events over the arms gives the simultaneous statement.
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency

nodes.name: Estimator consistency
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses, $\hat{\Theta}_n \to \Theta$ a.s., and consequently $\hat{\rho}_n \to v = \rho(\Theta)$ and $\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\to v_k$ a.s.
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency
nodes.label: lem:theta_consistent

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:all_arms_infinite} every arm is sampled infinitely often, so the first branch of Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_dichotomy} applies to every $k$: $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}\to\theta_k$. Continuity of $\rho$ gives $\hat{\rho}_n\to\rho(\Theta)=v$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:match} the limit $u$ of $N_n/n$ equals $v$. \emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.theta\_consistent\_pi\_of\_condB} discharges this from the \emph{joint} consistency (a common a.s.\ limit $u$ with both $N_{n,k}/n\to u_k$ and $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$) plus Condition~\textbf{B}: since $\hat\rho_{n,k}=\rho(\hat{\Theta}_n)_k\to \rho(z)_k$ ($z$ the estimator-vector limit) the shared limit is $u=\rho(z)$, which Condition~\textbf{B}'s non-sparsity (\texttt{hTpos}, Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges}) makes positive; positivity gives $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ (\texttt{all\_arms\_infinite}), so the dichotomy's infinite branch (\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_of\_pullCount\_atTop}) identifies each limit as the arm mean. For an aRTS design the joint consistency is exactly \texttt{aRTS\_consistency\_of\_isARTS} (whose plug-in target \texttt{aRTSTarget} is by definition $\rho(\hat{\Theta}_n)$), giving the fully discharged \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_theta\_consistent}: $\hat{\Theta}_n\to\Theta$ a.s.\ under only the aRTS design hypotheses and Condition~\textbf{B}. (\texttt{AlphaRAR.theta\_consistent} is the per-arm core taking the positive proportion as hypothesis.)
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency

nodes.name: LIL rate for the estimator
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses, $\hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta = O\!\big(\sqrt{\tfrac{\log\log n}{n}}\big)$ a.s. (the sharp $\log\log$ rate; a coarser $\log$ form is also formalized). The formalized statement \texttt{abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_loglog\_of\_proportion} assembles the pathwise core: from the exact error identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}), the two-sided $\log\log$ bound $|Q_{n,k}|\le C\sqrt{n\log\log n}$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:subsampled_lil}, converted from the pull count $N_{n,k}$ to the time index $n$ via $N_{n,k}\sim v_k n$) and $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k>0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:match}), it gives $|\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k|\le C'\,\sqrt{n\log\log n}/n = C'\sqrt{\log\log n/n}$ for large $n$.
nodes.label: lem:theta_LIL

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur} the error is exactly $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k = (Q_{n,k}+(\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k))/(N_{n,k}+1)$. Optional skipping turns $Q_{\cdot,k}$ into a predictably subsampled i.i.d.\ partial sum, so the subsampled Hartman--Wintner LIL (Corollary~\ref{cor:subsampled_lil}) gives $|Q_{n,k}| = O(\sqrt{N_{n,k}\log\log N_{n,k}})$ a.s.; since $N_{n,k}\sim v_k n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:match}), eventually $N_{n,k}\le 2v_k n$ and $\log\log N_{n,k}\le 2\log\log n$, whence $|Q_{n,k}| = O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ (\texttt{ae\_eventually\_abs\_respMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog}). Dividing by $N_{n,k}+1 \gtrsim (v_k/2)n$ bounds $|\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k| \le (2/v_k)(C+|\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k|)\sqrt{n\log\log n}/n = O(\sqrt{\log\log n / n})$, via the shared deterministic core \texttt{abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_gen}. The coarser $\log$-rate route through the truncation LIL (Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_truncation}, \texttt{abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_ae}) remains available.

nodes.name: Rate for the plug-in target
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses, $\hat{\rho}_n - v = O\!\big(\sqrt{\tfrac{\log\log n}{n}}\big)$ and hence $n(\hat{\rho}_n - v) = O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s.
nodes.label: lem:rho_rate

nodes.statement: A first-order Taylor expansion of $\rho$ around $\Theta$ (twice differentiable by Condition~\textbf{B}) gives $\hat{\rho}_n - v = G(\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta) + O(\|\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta\|^2)$ with $G := \nabla\rho|_\Theta$. Both terms are $O(\sqrt{\log\log n / n})$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL}. \emph{Formalization.} The delta-method core is formalized as \texttt{AlphaRAR.rho\_rate}: for a target map $\rho$ merely \emph{differentiable} at $\Theta$ (the first-order part of Condition~\textbf{B}; the second-order term is unnecessary for the $O$-rate), if the estimator vector converges, $\hat{\Theta}_n\to\Theta$ a.s.\ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_consistent}), with each coordinate at the rate $\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k = O(r_n)$ a.s.\ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL}, $r_n=\sqrt{\log\log n/n}$), then every coordinate of the plug-in target satisfies $\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k = O(r_n)$ a.s. The mechanism is the generic estimate \texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_target\_sub\_of\_tendsto}: a differentiable map sends $\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta$ to $\rho(\hat{\Theta}_n)-\rho(\Theta)$ of the same big-$O$ order (\texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_sub\_comp\_of\_differentiableAt}, from \texttt{HasFDerivAt.isBigO\_sub}), combined coordinatewise via \texttt{isBigO\_pi}. For a concrete aRTS design this is fully discharged in \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_rho\_rate}: consistency $\hat{\Theta}_n\to\Theta$ is \texttt{aRTS\_theta\_consistent} (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_consistent}) and the coordinatewise rate is the subsampled loglog LIL (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL}), fed through the positive allocation proportion, so the only remaining hypotheses are Condition~\textbf{B} (differentiability and non-sparsity) and the Condition~\textbf{A} moments.

nodes.name: Strong consistency and rates
nodes.statement: Under the generic conditions and Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for every $k\in[K]$, as $n\to\infty$, \[ \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\xrightarrow{a.s.} v_k, \qquad \hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta = O\!\Big(\sqrt{\tfrac{\log\log n}{n}}\Big)\ \text{a.s.},\qquad n(\hat{\rho}_n - v) = O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\ \text{a.s.} \]
nodes.label: thm:LLN

nodes.statement: Combine Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_consistent} (first statement), Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL} (second) and Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_rate} (third). The formalization \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_LLN} bundles the conclusions for an aRTS design: $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ (\texttt{aRTS\_proportion\_tendsto}), $\hat\theta_{n,k}\to\theta_k$ (\texttt{aRTS\_theta\_consistent}), $\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k=O(\sqrt{\log\log n/n})$ (\texttt{aRTS\_theta\_rate}, the Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL} rate instantiated for aRTS through the positive allocation proportion) and $\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k=O(\sqrt{\log\log n/n})$ (\texttt{aRTS\_rho\_rate}), under the aRTS design hypotheses and Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}.

nodes.name: Additive decomposition of the $U$-increment
nodes.statement: For any non-decreasing sequence $(\ell_n)$ with $\ell_n\le n$, under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for each $k$, \[ U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_n,k} = (n-\ell_n)\big[-(1-\alpha)v_k + o(1)\big] + (M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_n,k}) + \ell_n\big(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n,k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}\big). \]
nodes.label: lem:diff_U_decomp

nodes.statement: Expanding $U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_n,k}$ from Definition~\ref{def:U} and grouping the target terms around $v_k$, $U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_n,k} = (n-\ell_n)\big[-(1-\alpha)v_k - (\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k) + \frac{\alpha}{n-\ell_n}\sum_{m=\ell_n}^{n-1}(\hat{\rho}_{m,k}-v_k)\big] + M_{n,k}-M_{\ell_n,k} + \ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n,k}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}, $\hat{\rho}_n\to v$, so both $\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k$ and the Cesàro average $\frac1{n-\ell_n}\sum_{m=\ell_n}^{n-1}(\hat{\rho}_{m,k}-v_k)$ are $o(1)$ (treating separately the bounded and diverging cases of $\ell_n$). \emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.diff\_U\_decomp}. The exact $M$-explicit identity is \texttt{AlphaRAR.auxU\_sub}; the $o(1)$ remainder $\alpha\sum_{[\ell_n,n)}(\hat\rho_m-v) -(n-\ell_n)(\hat\rho_n-v)$ is made rigorous as ``for every $\varepsilon>0$, eventually $|\cdot|\le\varepsilon(n-\ell_n)$'', its first term controlled by the windowed Cesàro bound \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_sum\_Ico\_sub\_le\_of\_tendsto} (valid for an arbitrary window, bounded or diverging) and its second by $\hat\rho_n\to v$.

nodes.name: Control of $\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)$
nodes.statement: Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B} there is a constant $C\ge0$ with, for any non-decreasing $(\ell_n)$, $\ell_n\le n$, \[ \big|\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n} - \hat{\rho}_n)\big| \le o(1)(n-\ell_n) + C\|Q_n - Q_{\ell_n}\| + o_p(\sqrt n). \]
nodes.label: lem:ell_rho_control

nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_Op}, $Q_{n,k}=O_p(\sqrt n)$, hence $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k = Q_{n,k}/N_{n,k} + o_p(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}) = O_p(n^{-1/2})$ using $N_{n,k}\sim v_k n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_error_Q}). The Taylor expansion of $\rho$ gives $\hat{\rho}_n - v = G(\hat{\Theta}_n-\Theta)+O_p(1/n)$ and similarly at $\ell_n$; subtracting, $\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n) = \ell_n G(\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\Theta}_n) + O_p(1)$, so $|\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)| \le C\ell_n\|\hat{\Theta}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\Theta}_n\| + O_p(1)$. Writing the estimator difference through $Q$ (splitting into the increment $\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^n$ and the reweighting of $\sum_{j\le\ell_n}$) and bounding each piece using $N_{n,k}-N_{\ell_n,k}\le n-\ell_n$ and the SLLN, the three resulting terms are respectively $C\|Q_n-Q_{\ell_n}\|$, $o(1)(n-\ell_n)$ and $o_p(\sqrt n)$. \emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.ell\_rho\_control} produces the bound in the shape $\ell_n|\hat\rho_{\ell_n,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}| \le V_\rho(n-\ell_n)+W_\rho$ with $V_\rho=o_p(1)$, $W_\rho=o_p(\sqrt n)$, which is what the drift-sign step consumes. The Condition-\textbf{B} input enters as the single hypothesis \texttt{hlip} (the target is Lipschitz near $\Theta$, so $|\hat\rho_{\ell,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}|\le L\sum_{k'}|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|$ eventually) --- mirroring how \texttt{clt\_rho} takes the derivative as a hypothesis. The estimator-increment control $\ell|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|\le g_{k'}(n-\ell)+h_{k'} |Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|$ is \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_estimator\_diff\_le}; the coefficients are $g_{k'}=o_p(1)$ (from the Doob-maximal bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_sup'\_abs\_div\_sqrt} and the a.s.\ bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}) and the reweighting coefficient $h_{k'}=\ell_n/(N_{n,k'}+1)$, which is only \emph{bounded in probability} ($O_p(1)$, converging a.s.\ to $1/v_{k'}$, again via \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}), not by a uniform constant; it therefore enters the $o_p$ bookkeeping through $O_p\cdot o_p=o_p$ (\texttt{IsBigOpOne.mul\_littleOp}). The $Q$-increment control $|Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|\le Q_v(n-\ell)+Q_w$ is \texttt{qm\_increments\_resp}.

nodes.name: $Q$- and $M$-increments are $o_p(\sqrt n)$ plus drift
nodes.statement: Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for the hitting time $\ell_{n,k}$, \[ \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \le o_p(1)(n-\ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt n), \qquad |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| \le o_p(1)(n-\ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt n). \]
nodes.label: lem:QM_increments

nodes.statement: Pick $L_n\to\infty$ with $L_n = o(n)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} and Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_dyadic} bound the two maximal quantities $\mathbb{E}[\max_{m\le L_n}\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|]\le 2\sqrt{L_n C_0}$ and $\mathbb{E}[\max_{L_n\le m<n}\frac{\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|}{m}]\le 3\sqrt{C_0/L_n}$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:expectation_to_O} these are $O_p(\sqrt{L_n})=o_p(\sqrt n)$ and $O_p(1/\sqrt{L_n})=o_p(1)$ respectively. Plugging into the deterministic inequality of Lemma~\ref{lem:increment_control} gives the bound for $Q$; the same argument applied to $M$ gives the second bound. \emph{Formalization.} The two maximal quantities are formalized as \texttt{wmaxSeq} and \texttt{vmaxSeq} (with the concrete window $L_n=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$), and the two $o_p$ statements are \texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_wmaxSeq\_div\_sqrt} ($o_p(\sqrt n)$) and \texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_vmaxSeq} ($o_p(1)$), proved from the \emph{vector} maximal bounds (Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_pi}) and Markov's inequality. The deterministic increment control is \texttt{AlphaRAR.norm\_increment\_le\_vmaxSeq\_wmaxSeq}. For $Q$ (the response martingale, a square-integrable family) the $o_p$ statements are \texttt{AlphaRAR.qm\_increments\_resp}; for the scalar assignment martingale $M$ (bounded increments $|\Delta M|\le1$) they are \texttt{AlphaRAR.qm\_increments\_of\_bdd} (via the singleton family $\{M\}$).

nodes.name: Upper bound on the $U$-increment
nodes.statement: Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for every $k$, \[ U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le o_p(\sqrt n), \qquad U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\ \text{a.s.} \] The $o_p(\sqrt n)$ half is formalized (generically) as \texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_max\_of\_decomp}; the a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ half is formalized (for the $\alpha\text{RTS}$ objects, inline) inside \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_dev\_upper} --- the $U$-increment decomposition \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp} with $\varepsilon=(1-\alpha)v_k/2$ makes the drift $\le0$, and the $M$- and $\rho$-differences are $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s.\ by the assignment-martingale LIL (Cor.~\ref{cor:llil_nat}) and the plug-in-target rate (Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_rate}).
nodes.label: lem:U_increment_bound

nodes.statement: From Lemma~\ref{lem:ell_rho_control} and the $Q$-bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:QM_increments}, $|\ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})| \le o_p(1)(n-\ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt n)$. Substituting this and the $M$-bound into the decomposition of Lemma~\ref{lem:diff_U_decomp}, $U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_{n,k},k} = (n-\ell_{n,k})[-(1-\alpha)v_k+o_p(1)] + o_p(\sqrt n) \le o_p(\sqrt n)$, since the drift coefficient is $\le0$ and $n-\ell_{n,k}\ge0$. For the a.s.\ bound, Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} gives $n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$, hence $\ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$, and the LIL for the martingale $M$ gives $M_{n,k}=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$; the same substitution yields the second inequality.

nodes.name: Deviation between proportions and plug-in target
nodes.statement: Under the generic conditions and Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for every $k$, \begin{align*} |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= o_p(\sqrt n), & |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\ \text{a.s.}, \\ N_{n,k} - n v_k &= O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\ \text{a.s.} \end{align*} \emph{Formalization.} The generic $o_p(\sqrt n)$ assembly is \texttt{AlphaRAR.prop\_dev}: for a finite family with $\sum_k \mathrm{Dev}_k = 0$ (\texttt{sum\_count\_sub\_smul\_eq\_zero}), the generic inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}, and the $U$-increment decomposition (drift $-(1-\alpha)v_k$, the $M$- and $\rho$-terms increment-controlled by \texttt{qm\_increments\_of\_bdd} and \texttt{ell\_rho\_control}, and an $o_p(1)$ perturbation from \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp}), it yields $\mathrm{Dev}_k=o_p(\sqrt n)$ via the drift-sign lemma \texttt{isLittleOpOne\_max\_div\_sqrt\_of\_drift} and the simplex reverse step \texttt{isLittleOpOne\_dev\_of\_sum\_zero}. The concrete paper-form statement $|N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k}|=o_p(\sqrt n)$ is \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_prop\_dev}, the full, self-contained $\alpha\text{RTS}$ instantiation: from the $\alpha\text{RTS}$ design bundle (an \texttt{IsAlgEnvSeq} sequence, Condition \textbf{A} $Y\in L^2$, a continuous simplex-valued target $\rho$, the algorithm-level predicate \texttt{IsARTS} --- whence the throttle via \texttt{throttle\_of\_isARTS} ---, $\alpha\in[0,1)$, Condition \textbf{B} ($\rho$ Lipschitz near $\Theta$ and non-sparsity $0<v_k$), and the $\mathrm{thm{:}LLN}$ consistencies $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ and $\hat{\Theta}_n\to\Theta$), it discharges \emph{every} hypothesis of \texttt{prop\_dev} internally: the generic inequality via \texttt{generic\_ineq\_of\_hitting} (a.e., from the throttle), the smallness via \texttt{preliminary\_small}, the $M$-increment via the seam $M=\texttt{assignMart}$ (\texttt{assignMart\_eq\_assignMG}) and \texttt{qm\_increments\_of\_bdd}, the \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp} perturbation shown $o_p$ (a.e.\ $\to0$ by $\hat\rho_n\to v$), and the plug-in-target increment control (Lemma~\ref{lem:ell_rho_control}) via \texttt{ell\_rho\_control}, whose $g$- and $h$-coefficients are the random-hitting-time bounds \texttt{aRTS\_g\_littleOp} ($O_p\cdot o_p=o_p$, Doob running-max plus $\sqrt n/(N_n+1)\to0$) and \texttt{aRTS\_h\_bigOp} (a.s.\ bounded). All random-hitting-time terms are made measurable by \texttt{measurable\_eval\_of\_le}. The two a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ statements are also formalized, as \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_prop\_dev\_ae} ($N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k}=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s.) and \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_count\_sub\_smul\_ae} ($N_{n,k}-nv_k=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s.). The a.s.\ route is \emph{simpler} than the $o_p$ one --- it bypasses the entire \texttt{ell\_rho\_control} / \texttt{vmaxSeq} maximal-inequality machinery, resting instead on two pointwise a.s.\ loglog rates: the assignment-martingale LIL \texttt{AlphaRAR.ae\_eventually\_abs\_assignMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog} ($M_{n,k}=O(\sqrt{n\log \log n})$ a.s.) and the plug-in-target rate \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_rho\_rate} ($\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n}/n)$ a.s.). For each arm, \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_dev\_upper} combines the key inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}, the smallness $\le 0$ (\texttt{preliminary\_small}), and the $U$-increment decomposition \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp} with $\varepsilon=(1-\alpha)v_k/2$ (so the drift is $\le0$): the $M$- and $\rho$-differences at the random time $\ell_{n,k}\le n$ are controlled uniformly by \texttt{AlphaRAR.exists\_forall\_le\_mul\_sqrt\_mul\_log\_log} (``$O(\sqrt{m\log\log m})$ at every $m\le n$ is $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$''), giving a one-sided $N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k}\le O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$; the reverse step \texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_of\_forall\_upper\_of\_sum\_zero} (using $\sum_k \mathrm{Dev}_k=0$) upgrades it to the two-sided bound, and $N_{n,k}-nv_k$ adds $n(\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k)$ via \texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_natMul\_sqrt\_mul\_log\_log}.
nodes.label: lem:prop_dev

nodes.statement: The generic inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq} together with \eqref{eq:generic_small} and Lemma~\ref{lem:U_increment_bound} gives the one-sided bounds $N_{n,k}-n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \le o_p(\sqrt n)$ and $\le O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s. The reverse inequality follows from $\sum_j N_{n,j}=n$, $\sum_j\hat{\rho}_{n,j}=1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:counts_sum}): $n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-N_{n,k}=\sum_{j\ne k}(N_{n,j}-n\hat{\rho}_{n,j})$, which inherits the same one-sided bounds. Combining gives the absolute-value statements. The last line adds $n(\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k)=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}.

nodes.name: Componentwise joint CLT
nodes.statement: Consider any RAR procedure whose pull counts are \emph{regular}: for every $k$ there is a deterministic sequence $c_{k,n}\to\infty$ with \[ \frac{N_{n,k}}{c_{k,n}}\xrightarrow{a.s.}1 . \] Under Condition~\textbf{A}, with $D_n := \mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{N_{n,1}},\dots,\sqrt{N_{n,K}})$, \[ D_n(\hat{\Theta}_n - \Theta) \overset{\mathcal{D}}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{N}\!\big(0, \mathrm{diag}(V_1,\dots,V_K)\big). \] No positivity of the limiting proportions is required, so this covers \emph{sparse} arms $v_k=0$.
nodes.section: 7.3 Joint central limit theorem for the estimators
nodes.label: lem:componentwise

nodes.name: The regularity hypothesis is necessary
nodes.statement: The weaker hypothesis ``$N_{n,k}\to\infty$ a.s.'' does \emph{not} suffice when the index is chosen adaptively. Take one arm with i.i.d.\ $\mathcal N(\theta,V)$ responses; by the law of the iterated logarithm $\limsup_m S_m/\sqrt{Vm}=+\infty$ a.s., so an algorithm may pull the arm until $S_M/\sqrt{VM}>1$, then pause it for the next $M$ rounds, and repeat forever.
